_comment: Tier-2: FSI needs FluidDynamics + StructuralMechanics + MeshMoving + Mapping. A negative control (NoSuchKratosApplication) proves the import probe discriminates.  Pitfall (kratos.fsi #1). NOTE ON THE WRITTEN SIGNAL: this claim carries one of the five shared boilerplate Signal suffixes used across the Kratos catalog, which does not describe what actually happens. The real signal is recorded below and in the fixture output. Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv on external ext4 image). All four import, plus FSIApplication itself. The claim is the same hidden-dependency fact as _auxiliary_overview #1 but stated from the FSI side; both are pinned so a stack that drops MeshMoving or Mapping — neither of which appears in a user-facing FSI JSON — fails this fixture rather than failing opaquely at runtime inside partitioned_fsi_base_solver. The fixture imports KratosMultiphysics at module scope; with Kratos absent the import raises, the process exits non-zero and the runner records a failure, never a pass.
